brief: Design an interface for a "Silent Auction of Unspoken Words"—a therapeutic tool where users compose messages they'll never send, then watch as an AI bidding system assigns emotional weight values to t

dominant_strengths: Restrained minimalism gives the composing area a quiet, confessional feel appropriate to the therapeutic premise of unspoken words
Clear left-rail compose / right-stage auction split establishes a legible mental model before any interaction begins
Tiny tracked-caps labels ('LIVE BIDDING', 'WORDS DISSOLVED INTO VOID') hint at a poetic editorial voice worth developing
dominant_weaknesses: Right 70% of canvas is literally empty—no auction visualization, no bid stream, no emotional-weight system shown, so the core concept is invisible
Flat grey-on-grey palette and absence of any motion or texture make the 'auction' feel inert rather than alive or dissolving
Black solid CTA button clashes tonally with the airy ghostly aesthetic; it reads like a generic form, not a ritual release
fix_priorities: Populate the right stage with a live bid feed, weight values, and dissolving word typography to actually express the concept
Replace the harsh black button with a softer ritual gesture (long-press, drag-to-release) matching the dissolution metaphor
Introduce subtle motion: words drifting, fading, or being outbid, to give the auction temporal presence
Add typographic hierarchy contrast—an elegant serif for unspoken text vs the mono caps system layer
rationale.norman_balance: Reflective intent is strongest, but visceral atmosphere and behavioral feedback are both underdeveloped, leaving the concept conceptual rather than felt.
rationale.intent_fit: Partially fits—the compose surface exists, but the auction, bidding, and emotional-weight systems that define the brief are absent from view.
